label: Chunky voxel
blurb: Pixel 3 with two toon bands, a 1-art-pixel hull rim and a dark ring around every tile top; the flattest, most graphic option, but two bands throw away most of the sculpts’ modelling.

label: Chunky sprite
blurb: Painted sprites with a dilated near-black outline over the same ringed tiles; the crispest silhouettes of the nine, at the cost of the pieces never turning with the camera.

label: Chunky + Endesga 32
blurb: Chunky voxel quantised to the Endesga-32 ramp for saturated poster colour; the strongest graphic unity, but the ramp swallows the tile edge ring on dark squares and pulls both armies toward the same navy.

label: Dungeon sprite
blurb: Painted sprites on Drive stone tiles under four warm corner torches at 60°, with contact shadows; the most atmospheric, but the far corners go dark enough to hurt piece identification.

label: Dungeon voxel
blurb: Same stone board and torches with voxel sculpts, so the pieces catch the warm light in 3D; the light falloff costs contrast on the dark army more than the sprites do.

label: Dungeon bright
blurb: Stone tiles and contact shadows under the existing bright paper lighting; keeps reference B’s textured floor and full readability, but loses the torch mood entirely.

label: Iso voxel
blurb: True 45°/30° isometric on a tall board block with visible side faces, warm 32-colour ramp and a hull rim; the strongest sense of place, but a 30° camera makes front pieces occlude the rank behind.

label: Iso sprite
blurb: The iso board with outlined painted sprites on the warm ramp; the closest match to the reference art, though billboards at 30° stand oddly tall against the flat board.

label: Iso clean
blurb: Iso camera and tall board with no palette quantisation, so the painted voxel colours survive; clearer piece colour than C1, but it loses the limited-palette cohesion the reference lives on.
